page: Microsoft Azure D2s_v3 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DSv3 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The configuration provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading, resulting in 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB per core, and includes a 16 GB local SSD. The instance is also Premium Storage capable, allowing for external storage upgrades.

Benchmark evaluations place this instance in the lower performance tiers. In CPU-focused tests, the stress-ng single-core performance scored 1238.89, placing it in the bottom 25%, while multi-core performance registered at 1629.2, which is in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large-block read-only bandwidth at 13.15 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 10.79 GB/sec, both falling into the bottom 10%. Database and web serving capabilities are similarly limited, with Redis SET operations achieving 1.55 million operations per second and static web serving throughput reaching 1.68 GB/sec.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation but lower-tier benchmark results, the D2s_v3 represents an entry-level general-purpose resource. It offers a predictable hardware profile with dedicated vCPUs at a lower resource density, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that require dedicated compute but do not demand high memory bandwidth or intensive processing power. It is best suited for light general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, small-scale development or testing environments, and low-throughput background tasks.
